name: OmaPodman
author: Abdullah Mansoor
description: Podman in the Omarchy bar: containers, images, volumes and networks on four tabs. Live CPU and memory, start/stop/restart, logs and a shell without a terminal, and one keystroke to reclaim whatever nothing is using.

barWidget.description: Four tabs — containers grouped by Compose project with live CPU and memory, plus images, volumes and networks sorted biggest-first with the unused ones on top and a prune button that says what it is about to delete. Driven from the keyboard: 1-4 or h/l jump between tabs, j/k move, enter starts or stops, o tails the logs, s opens a shell, r restarts, x removes, p prunes, c copies, / filters, u refreshes, d opens podman-tui, and ? lists the lot inside the panel.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often the bar glyph re-reads Podman. The panel refreshes every 3 seconds while it is open, regardless of this.

schema.label: Tab the panel opens on
schema.description: Where the panel lands every time it opens. Press 1-4, or h and l, to move between tabs once it is open.

schema.label: Show stopped containers
schema.description: Off lists only running containers, which keeps the panel short on a machine with a long history of one-off runs.

schema.label: Show CPU and memory
schema.description: Off skips the podman stats call entirely. Worth turning off on a laptop: sampling every running container costs about a second of work each time the panel is open.

schema.label: Measure what each volume costs
schema.description: Asks Podman to walk every volume on disk, which takes a second or two on a busy machine. Off keeps the volume list instant and leaves the per-volume sizes blank; the reclaimable total in the footer still works either way.

schema.label: Hide the bar icon when there are no containers
schema.description: On removes the button from the bar until Podman has something to show.
